channel.title: Orbital Notes
channel.description: Space news and backyard astronomy from the Southern Hemisphere.

item.title: Spotting the International Space Station from the suburbs
item.description: It is the brightest thing moving across the sky after sunset, and you need nothing more than a pass-prediction app and a clear western horizon. This week has three good evening passes.

item.title: The Orionids peak this month: how to watch
item.description: Debris from Halley's Comet gives us a steady shower in late October. From southern latitudes the radiant rises after midnight, so the best viewing is in the hours before dawn.

item.title: Finding the Southern Cross, and the pointers that lead to it
item.description: A beginner's guide to the constellation on the flag. Look for the two bright pointer stars first; the cross itself is smaller than most people expect.

item.title: Reading an exoplanet spectrum without a physics degree
item.description: When a planet crosses its star, a sliver of starlight passes through its atmosphere. The dips in that light tell us which molecules are there. We decode one chart, step by step.

item.title: Why reusable rockets land on barges
item.description: Flying back to the launch site costs fuel that could have gone into payload. Landing downrange at sea is the compromise, and the numbers behind it are surprisingly simple.

item.title: A cheap first telescope for kids that actually gets used
item.description: Skip the department-store refractor with the wobbly tripod. A small tabletop reflector shows the rings of Saturn and the craters of the Moon, and it sets up in a minute.

item.title: What the Moon's far side really looks like
item.description: It is not dark, just unseen from here. Fewer maria, more craters, and a thicker crust: a short tour of the hemisphere that always faces away from us.
